approved_payload.content: A North West businessman was charged on 21 October and first appeared in the Musina Magistrate's Court on 22 October, added as a co-accused in a case over two vehicles intercepted at the Beitbridge border post on 22 July (Limpopo Mirror and Review Online, 22 October). According to police and the NPA, police at the border post intercepted two vehicles, still financed by Absa, that were allegedly being taken from Mahikeng to Malawi; lawful bank authorisation to move them across the border was allegedly not obtained and fraudulent bank documents were allegedly arranged instead. Two people were arrested in July and remain in custody, due in the Musina Regional Court on 27 October; the vehicles were handed back to Absa. The NPA alleges the businessman acted in collusion with his employees. The reported charges differ: Limpopo Mirror lists attempted theft and fraud, Review Online attempted theft and money laundering. These are allegations: no one has been convicted, and the accused are not named here. Case status: charged and appeared in court; the reports do not give a consistent next date for his case, so none is stated here. Two outlets, both resting on police and NPA statements. The pin marks the South African border control at Beitbridge, where the July interception happened; the October charge and court appearance were not at this point, and the July date is the alleged conduct, not the pin date.
